title: Duchy of Warsaw
capsule: The Duchy of Warsaw was a French client state established by Napoleon Bonaparte under the Treaty of Tilsit (1807) from Prussian-held Polish territories, with Frederick Augustus I of Saxony as duke. Its constitution, drawn up by Napoleon, introduced the Napoleonic Code and abolished serfdom, making it a vehicle for Polish national aspirations within the imperial system. The duchy expanded significantly after the Treaty of Schönbrunn (1809), when it gained Galician territories from Austria. After Napoleon's defeat, the Congress of Vienna (1815) dissolved the duchy, converting most of its territory into the Congress Kingdom of Poland under Russian suzerainty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution.
